    feat(macapp): give every workroom its own title bar and toolbar
    
    Closes #139.
    
    A workroom only had its own chrome when it was part of a split group, and its
    run/"Open in…" controls lived in the window title bar keyed on the *selected*
    target — so a co-displayed split member's were unreachable, and
    `runOrFocusRunCommand()` read the selection, meaning a per-member Run button
    would have started the run in the wrong workroom.
    
    Now every workroom renders as a card with its own header and its own trailing
    toolbar, and the window title bar keeps only window-level chrome (sidebar
    toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal).
    
    Because the header became unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` LOST most of its
    `multi` branching rather than gaining more: with no `if` there is no
    `_ConditionalContent` branch left to flip when a split dissolves, so the
    libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis is gone. `multi` now survives in four
    leaf-level places only — the remove-from-split ✕, its menu item, the group-drag
    gesture mask, and the a11y `.isSelected` trait.
    
    Solo and split geometry are identical (6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset), which
    made the `compact` parameter permanently true, so it is deleted across four
    files. The card's accent tint goes neutral when the window isn't key.
    
    Run is now per-target: `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` carries the state machine
    and the selection-scoped overload delegates to it. `isEditingTextField` stays on
    the selection door only, which also fixes a latent bug — a Run *click* while the
    sidebar filter held focus used to no-op, because that guard was written for
    ambient ⌘R. The button is shown even with no run command configured; pressing it
    opens Project Settings with the warning, the same branch ⌘R has used since #127.
    
    Notable fixes found while building it:
    
    - `GestureMask.none` would have shipped dead buttons. The header carries the
      group-drag gesture, and `.none` disables every gesture in the SUBVIEW
      hierarchy as well as the added one — solo, that kills the header's own Run and
      Open-in. Hover is `.onHover`, not a gesture, so they would have looked alive.
      `.subviews` drops only the drag.
    - A solo missing-directory workroom never reached `WorkroomSplitView` at all
      (`RootView` had its own `isMissing` branch), so "always" was false for it.
      `TargetTerminalDetail` now owns that state for every pane as a ZStack sibling,
      not a structural branch under a live surface.
    - The "Open in…" icon ignored its own `.frame`: it was a hidden SF Symbol with
      the icon in an `.overlay`, and an overlay takes its base's size, so the icon
      rendered at whatever the ambient font made the symbol. It is sized directly now.
    - `ExternalEditor.installed` was an uncached computed property doing three
      LaunchServices lookups per evaluation, about to run once per visible pane;
      `icon` mutated the size of an image `NSWorkspace` may share. Both cached, and
      the icon is drawn into a fresh image.
    - Divider-drag ratios are held in local `@State` and committed on mouse-up
      instead of publishing to the store per mouse-moved tick, which rebuilt every
      pane at cursor rate.
    - Chip-drop hit-testing planned against the unpadded detail rect while the
      renderer plans inside the gutter, so a drop in the gutter split with no preview.
    
    `SplitPaneUITests` asserted a collapsed split leaves ZERO title bars; it now
    leaves one, and the ✕ is what distinguishes collapsed from still-split.
    `TabReorderMathTests`' compact-inset case no longer describes a distinction the
    app makes, so it is restated as plain arithmetic.
    
    Running the new XCUITests then surfaced a latent bug in the SHARED tab-strip
    scroller, which this change is the first to reach. `OverflowingTabScroller` pins
    its "+" via `safeAreaInset(edge: .trailing)`, whose `spacing:` sits between the
    CHIPS and the "+" — leaving the "+" flush with the scroller's trailing edge, and
    `TerminalTabStrip`'s outer `HStack(spacing: 0)` put the per-tab toolbar's first
    button at exactly that x (measured: both at 1123). That is symptom 1 of issue
    #129, "no abutting". It hid because at the old strip width the default fixture's
    tabs still fit INLINE, where the gap was leftover slack; the new card geometry
    narrows the strip by 20pt, which pins them. The gutter is now explicit.
    
    Tests: 1374 unit, and 58 XCUITests across the new class plus every class this
    touches — pane header, split panes, run settings, tab-strip overflow, run status,
    workflow, tab actions, scroll-into-view, window drag, workrooms view. The
    real-mouse pass is still outstanding: hover and click on this bar are a known
    real-mouse-only bug class that synthetic events can't judge.

    feat(macapp): let a window hold several workroom split groups
    
    A window stored ONE workroom split layout (`AppStore.workroomSplit:
    PaneLayout<SidebarID>?`), so grouping two solo workrooms replaced the group you
    already had. It now stores a list (`workroomSplits`): groups coexist, are
    disjoint, hold >=2 leaves each, and exactly one is visible — the one holding the
    selection.
    
    - Splits join `beside`'s group or seed a new one; a moved member still leaves its
      old group first (collapse, or dissolve below two), so no duplicate leaf.
    - Remove / auto-close / prune are per group; the prune walks every group.
    - `setWorkroomSplitRatio` finds the owning group by split-node id (new
      `PaneLayout.containsSplit`); "Resize Workroom Splits Evenly" acts on the
      visible group.
    - `displayedWorkroomTargets` pulls each group into its own contiguous chip run,
      and the tab bar draws one bracket per group, dropping the hairline at every
      group boundary (including group A to group B).
    - Surface-focus routing and `onScreenTarget` key on the visible group, so a
      hidden group's stale focus claim can't steal the selection.
    - The reload self-heal takes the pre-validation selection: with several groups,
      re-pointing to the first survivor in array order landed you in a split you were
      never viewing.
    
    Coverage: 12 new store tests (coexistence, cross-group moves, per-group
    remove/ratio/equalize/prune, prune re-point, visible-group reads, hidden-group
    focus), a `containsSplit` tree test, and an XCUITest that hops between two
    seeded groups (`-WorkroomUITestSecondWorkroomSplit`) — it fails when the fixture
    emulates the old single-split store.

128	/// Geometry of a split group's contiguous chip run within a strip — the `x`/`width` of the rounded
129	/// bracket drawn around the members (issue #3). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip.splitRunRect` so the
130	/// arithmetic is unit-testable without a view, and so it shares one summation with
131	/// `TabStripOverflow.runWidth` instead of carrying a second copy of it.
132	enum TabStripSplitRun {
133	  /// - Parameters:
134	  ///   - widths: position-indexed chip widths (`widths[i]` is the chip at position `i`).
135	  ///   - memberIndices: positions of the group's members. Guaranteed contiguous by the caller's
136	  ///     display order; only the first and last are used, so a stray gap is spanned rather than
137	  ///     rejected.
138	  ///   - spacing: the strip's inter-chip spacing.
139	  /// - Returns: `nil` when there's no real split (fewer than two members) or the indices are out of
140	  ///   range — both mean "draw no bracket".
141	  static func rect(widths: [CGFloat], memberIndices: [Int], spacing: CGFloat)
142	    -> (x: CGFloat, width: CGFloat)?
143	  {
144	    guard memberIndices.count >= 2,
145	      let first = memberIndices.min(), let last = memberIndices.max(),
146	      first >= 0, last < widths.count
147	    else { return nil }
148	    // x: everything before the first member, chips + the spacing that follows each of them.
149	    var x: CGFloat = 0
150	    for i in 0..<first { x += widths[i] + spacing }
151	    // width: the members' own chips, plus the spacing *between* them (one fewer gap than chips).
152	    var width: CGFloat = 0
153	    for i in first...last { width += widths[i] }
154	    width += spacing * CGFloat(last - first)
155	    return (x, width)
156	  }
